page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.3xlarge is a storage-focused virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores of an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 48.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. A key hardware characteristic is the inclusion of 35,433 GB of local HDD storage, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively low, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by average ratings in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth remains average for both small and large block read/write operations, though the overall PassMark memory score is weak.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.d1.3xlarge is its reliance on high-capacity local HDD storage rather than solid-state drives, which optimizes it for sequential data access and high-density storage rather than random I/O performance. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a high ratio of storage capacity to compute resources, making it a viable option for workloads requiring massive local data footprints without demanding top-tier single-threaded CPU performance. Suitable workloads include large-scale data warehousing, log processing, MapReduce jobs, and cold storage databases.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.3xlarge is a storage-oriented virtual server featuring 12 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It is configured with 48.0 GB of RAM and a substantial 35,433 GB of local HDD storage, supported by a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results show weak single-core CPU and memory performance, but average multi-core scaling across stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark tests. The instance represents a qualitative tradeoff, prioritizing massive local storage capacity over high-speed random I/O and single-threaded compute power. This hardware profile is best suited for storage-heavy workloads such as data warehousing, distributed file systems, log processing, and large-scale sequential data analysis where high-density local storage is required.
